facts.text: The README builds a Motor from the motor type, its Slave ID (the CAN id) and a Master ID that must be unique and not 0x00
The README opens the serial adapter with 921600 baud and a 0.5 s timeout and gives the port object to MotorControl
The README adds a motor to the MotorControl, enables it and documents disable as the way to switch the drive off
A Motor object holds the last feedback in state_q, state_dq and state_tau
recv_data(q, dq, tau) stores one feedback frame in the motor object
getPosition, getVelocity and getTorque return the stored feedback
A new Motor object starts in MIT control mode (NowControlMode = Control_Type.MIT)
A control method finds its motor by SlaveID in motors_map and returns without a command when the motor was not added
addMotor stores the motor under its SlaveID and, when that is not 0, under its MasterID too
control_Pos_Vel sends the desired position and velocity as float32 bytes on CAN id 0x100 + SlaveID
control_Vel sends the desired velocity as float32 bytes on CAN id 0x200 + SlaveID
enable, disable and set_zero_position send 0xFC, 0xFD and 0xFE as the last byte of an eight byte data frame
refresh_motor_status sends the status query and reads the answer back with recv()
switchControlMode writes the CTRL_MODE register and returns True when the motor reports the new value
The CTRL_MODE register is one of the integer registers (7 to 10, 13 to 16, 35 to 36), read and written as uint32
The CTRL_MODE register takes the integer range [1,4]
Control_Type maps MIT to 1, POS_VEL to 2, VEL to 3 and Torque_Pos to 4
A control mode change is temporary: the motor resets it after a power cycle
